findings.title: Concurrent index init races on shared err
findings.body: searchSupport.init launches one errgroup goroutine per namespace and each one does `_, _, err = s.build(...)` plus `totalBatchesIndexed++` on variables declared outside the loop. Those are unsynchronized shared writes. With BuildIndex no longer holding a process-wide lock, these goroutines actually run together, so a failed build can have its error overwritten by a later successful one (startup proceeds with a missing index) or a finished success can be overwritten by another goroutine's error (startup fails spuriously). The counter read for the trace event is likewise racy.

findings.title: Same-key index builds no longer serialized
findings.body: BuildIndex used to hold cacheMu for the whole build, which at least serialized bleve.New and cache publication. The lock is now taken only to assign b.cache[key]. getOrCreateIndex still does check-then-act (GetIndex, then build) with no per-key singleflight, and init can build many namespaces at once. Two callers for the same NamespacedResource can both pass GetIndex, both call bleve.New on the same directory (file indexes fail or corrupt the on-disk index), and the last cache write wins while the other caller keeps using the orphaned index. Searches and watch updates then diverge.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without the mutex
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache with no cacheMu held, while BuildIndex writes that map under cacheMu. searchSupport.init now starts the watch goroutine (which can BuildIndex a namespace that was below the init threshold) and then calls TotalDocs for the new startup log. A concurrent map write during that iteration panics the process.

findings.title: Failed constructor Init leaks lifecycle and in-flight builds
findings.body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init and, on error, returns nil without s.cancel() or lifecycle.Stop. Init runs lifecycle.Init (SQL backend opens the DB) before search.init. If index build fails, the caller has no server handle to stop the backend, so the DB pool is leaked. The cancelable context passed into the errgroup is also dropped, so in-flight namespace builds keep running after the constructor has already failed. Previously Init errors were returned on the live server, which could still be stopped.

findings.title: Search watch loop panics when the event channel closes
findings.body: After the index build, init always starts `for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) }` on context.Background(), not the server context. WatchWriteEvents' poller closes that channel when the SQL backend is stopped. A receive on a closed channel yields a nil *WrittenEvent, and handleEvent immediately reads evt.Type, which panics. Because init now runs inside NewResourceServer, every storage server starts this goroutine, and shutdown (server.Stop / backend cancel) will crash it. The goroutine also cannot be cancelled independently of the SQL poller.

findings.title: Storage-server startup test skipped on postgres
findings.body: TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer is the integration test that constructs and runs a storage-server target, which now builds the unified index inside NewResourceServer/InitializeModuleServer. The change skips that test whenever GRAFANA_TEST_DB=postgres, with a TODO that it fails in Drone. Postgres startup regressions from eager index init (the failure mode this PR is fixing) will not be caught in CI.

findings.title: BuildIndex span context is still discarded
findings.body: The PR's stated trace fix is to pass the span context into child work (`ctx, span := tracer.Start`). BuildIndex, which this change edits, still does `_, span := b.tracer.Start(...)`. The builder callback and SQL list work started from the incoming ctx are not children of the BuildIndex span, so the index-build trace stays disconnected from the work it wraps.
